season.title: Month by month
season.summary: Best waves: May to September and October, on south and southwest swells. High season for visitors is November to March, when the waves are smaller. From November to February you still don't need a wetsuit; a lycra helps at dawn.

tips.title: Before you land
faq.airport.q: How long is the drive from the airport?
faq.airport.a: About 45 minutes from Zihuatanejo airport (ZIH). A private transfer with Saladita Rentals is MX$1,500 each way, up to 4 people, and can stop on the way if you need it.
faq.cash.q: Is there an ATM, and how much cash should I bring?
faq.cash.a: There is one ATM in town, at Hacienda Café. About MX$1,000 a day is a comfortable spend, but bring what fits your trip — many places still prefer cash.
faq.signal.a: Telcel has the best signal. Most Saladita Rentals houses have Starlink, so you're not relying on the cell tower.
faq.water.a: No. The water is warm all year. From November to February you still don't need a wetsuit; a lycra or rashguard helps at dawn, around 5 or 6am.
faq.season.q: When are the waves best, and when is it busy?
faq.season.a: The best waves run from May to September and October. Winter, November to March, is high season for visitors, and the waves are smaller.
faq.beginner.q: Is La Saladita good for beginners?
faq.beginner.a: Yes. The main point, La Saladita, is the spot to learn, on a longboard. Rancho is for intermediates on long or short boards, and Boca is a beach break better suited to shortboards.
faq.lessons.q: Can I take surf lessons or rent a board?
faq.lessons.a: Yes. Message Saladita Rentals on WhatsApp with your level and your dates, and we'll set you up with a lesson or a board.
faq.firstday.q: Where should I eat on my first day?
faq.firstday.a: Morning: Hacienda Café, the only supermarket in town, with the ATM. Midday: fresh catch at Benny's. Sunset: Marea. Night: Acadia for theme nights and a good bar, or Angelina's in Los Llanos for typical Mexican food.
faq.safety.a: That reputation doesn't match daily life in La Saladita. For visitors it's a quiet town: people live here without problems, and that's how it feels.
